name: A financial year of a Bengaluru trading and services company registered in Karnataka, filing GSTR-3B monthly

documents.why: A purchase from a supplier registered in Karnataka, the company's own State: 18 % split into 3,600.00 of central tax and 3,600.00 of State tax, both credited in Table 4(A)(5), and a base that reaches no box because GSTR-3B has none for a taxable purchase.

The document this pack exists to prove: a supply inside Karnataka carries one code at 18 % and its postings split it in two — 9,000.00 of CGST in column 4 and 9,000.00 of SGST in column 5 of line 3.1(a), the 100,000.00 base in column 2.
The same rate to a customer in Maharashtra: an inter-State supply, so one posting of 9,000.00 of integrated tax in column 3 of line 3.1(a), and nothing in the central or State columns.
A purchase from Tamil Nadu at the merit rate: 1,000.00 of integrated tax credited in column 2 of Table 4(A)(5). Solar-powered devices are in Schedule I of Notification No. 9/2025, at 5 %.

An export of services under a Letter of Undertaking: no integrated tax, the 250,000.00 reaches line 3.1(b), and the credit behind it stays available — which is what makes a zero-rated supply different from an exempt one.

lines.name: Software development services, delivered to Chicago

documents.why: An exempt supply: the renting of a residential dwelling for use as a residence to an unregistered individual is exempt under Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate). No tax, 90,000.00 on line 3.1(c).

lines.name: Rent of the flat over the warehouse — six months

documents.why: A reverse charge: legal services of an advocate to a business entity are in Notification No. 13/2017-Central Tax (Rate), so the advocate charges nothing and the company owes 2,700.00 of CGST and 2,700.00 of SGST on line 3.1(d) and takes the same back in Table 4(A)(3). The supplier is owed 30,000.00, exactly the fee.

lines.name: Legal opinion on a supply contract

documents.why: An import of services: a cloud subscription from a supplier outside India. 10,800.00 of integrated tax owed on line 3.1(d) and credited in Table 4(A)(2), the supplier paid 60,000.00.

A blocked credit: repair of a passenger car used by a director falls under section 17(5)(ab). The 1,800.00 of tax is part of the cost, so account 6050 carries 11,800.00; the form still shows it in Table 4(A)(5) and takes it back in Table 4(B)(1).

lines.name: Service and repair of the director's car

documents.why: The second positive rate, inside the State: 5 % on solar lanterns, 500.00 of CGST and 500.00 of SGST.
A credit note under section 34 on the April services: line 3.1(a) goes down by 10,000.00 and its central and State columns by 900.00 each, in the month the note is dated in.

An import of goods: the integrated tax is assessed on the bill of entry and paid to customs, not to the seller. 14,400.00 credited in Table 4(A)(1), the same amount on the account the customs payment clears; the seller is owed 80,000.00.
Services to a customer in Delhi, a Union territory with a legislature and therefore a State for GST: inter-State, 21,600.00 of integrated tax.
An exempt purchase inside the State: printed books carry no tax, and Table 5 still asks for their value in its intra-State column.
A sale late in the year, unpaid at 31 March: it is what leaves a trade receivable on the closing balance sheet.

payments.why: The Karnataka supplier paid in full, tax included.
The intra-State invoice collected: 100,000.00 plus 9,000.00 plus 9,000.00.
The inter-State invoice collected: 50,000.00 plus 9,000.00 of integrated tax.
The export collected: with no tax on it, the amount received is the invoice.
The advocate paid the fee alone: under reverse charge the tax is the company's own to pay to the Government, not the supplier's.
A payment on account that settles nothing: an unmatched receipt is what an open-item ledger has to be able to hold.
